context:
Goal: merged branches and branch protection get handled without you doing each one.
Problem (rule): a cloud session cannot delete a branch or set branch protection, so a session on your computer does them under your grant, and the grant names claude-settings only.
Based on (measured): the refusals come from the cloud, not from our rules. At 20:55 CST the cloud's safety check refused triage's delete of a copied banchi branch, and at 22:18 CST the cloud's git proxy dropped the coordinator's branch delete. Branch protection needs GitHub admin rights the cloud lacks.
Based on (measured): closing a PR is not refused: a cloud session closed claude-settings #1162 through the GitHub tools at 22:16 CST. So the grant's third act, PR closes, is no longer needed.
Based on (read): your grant "Acts the cloud refuses" (2026-10-30 16:20 CDT) in .claude/CLAUDE.md. We wrote the grant; the cloud makes the refusals.
Departs from: that grant, which covers three acts for the claude-settings coordinator — it drops PR closes, and (a) lets any repo's coordinator ask, or (c) goes away.

lastAnswer.note: Asked: "theres three acts the cloud refuses and that was made by us, not by the cloud? why? should we remove it". Rewritten 22:18 CST: the refusals are the cloud's; the grant is ours; c added.

options.gain: Child repos clean up without asking you each time.
options.how: The grant names each repo's coordinator, for branch deletes and branch protection; PR closes leave it.
options.label: Two acts, any repo's coordinator
options.lose: More sessions can ask a session on your computer for these acts.

options.how: PR closes leave the grant; nothing else changes.
options.label: Two acts, claude-settings only
options.lose: Each child-repo branch delete waits on your word.

options.gain: No session on your computer acts on a coordinator's ask.
options.label: Remove the grant
options.lose: Every merged-branch delete and protection change in every repo comes to you.

title: The cloud itself refuses two cleanup acts; should a session on your computer do them for claude-settings only, for every repo, or not at all?
why: Recommended: a. The refusals are real and still happen, so removing the grant sends every cleanup back to you.
